The default `maxAge` is **172800000 ms, which is 2 days**. The Firecrawl "Fast scraping" docs say this twice:

- "Default freshness: `maxAge = 172800000` ms (2 days). If the cached copy is newer than this, it's returned instantly; otherwise, Firecrawl scrapes fresh and updates the cache." (https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/fast-scraping)
- "Default: `maxAge` is `172800000` (2 days)" (same page)

The v2 scrape API reference (https://docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/scrape) has a note that conflicts with this. It says "Default maxAge is extended to 2 years so existing cached pages remain eligible." The search excerpt didn't show which parameter or mode that note applies to. The 2-day figure is the one stated as the default in the feature docs. I didn't open the API reference page to resolve the conflict, so check it if you need the exact value for the v2 endpoint.
